title: Factory refuses any provider that is not Workers AI unless explicitly opted in
description: The gateway module accepts anthropic, openai and openrouter alongside workers-ai. Only Workers AI is billed on the Cloudflare invoice, which is where the operator credit lives; the other three are billed by the vendor in real cash. Nothing today prevents a config change or a typo from silently moving every run off credit-funded Workers AI onto a cash-billed vendor. Make workers-ai the only provider the factory will route to unless an explicit opt-in var names another, and state the billing consequence in the refusal message. Related: h4n guards the other direction (the gateway billing mode).
notes:
2026-08-21 09:57 - Measured context for this tick. An audit of every logged call through the operator's default AI Gateway found 981 calls: 938 on provider workers-ai ($50.19, Cloudflare invoice, credit-funded) and 35 on provider anthropic ($5.52, billed by the vendor in cash). The anthropic traffic was NOT this factory — the deployed Worker holds no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, so the route fails closed. That is exactly the problem: today's protection is the ABSENCE of a secret, not a decision. Adding a vendor key for any reason silently removes it. Both gateways currently report workers_ai_billing_mode=postpaid, which is the mode that reaches the invoice; h4n guards that half. See repo-wiki/cloud-factory-billing.md for the three-pot model.
